question: ap1

ideas.title: Washout-and-recall time course with inducible AP-1 degradation
ideas.description: Pulse a stimulus to activate AP-1, then acutely degrade c-Jun/c-Fos with an auxin- or dTAG-inducible system either during the pulse or only after washout. Track chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN), and transcription at AP-1-bound enhancers over days to weeks, then re-challenge with the same stimulus. If AP-1 is required for memory, degrading it after washout should erase the faster or stronger second response, while degradation during the initial pulse should not.

ideas.title: Enhancer motif knock-in to test whether AP-1 sites are necessary for retention
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or homology-directed repair to mutate the TGAC/TCA AP-1 motifs in the enhancers of memory-associated genes, leaving neighbouring sequence intact. Compare accessibility, H3K27ac, and priming of these loci after a stimulus and during a rest period, against wild-type and against sites that bind other factors. Persistence that depends on the intact motif would support AP-1 as the carrier of memory rather than a bystander.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage tracing of AP-1-experienced cells
ideas.description: Combine a Fos-driven recombinase or TRAP reporter with a heritable lineage barcode and single-cell multiome (scRNA + scATAC) to tag cells that activated AP-1 during a stimulus. Follow these cells after washout and during re-stimulation to ask whether the tagged subset is a stable, heterogeneous population that responds faster, and whether memory is carried by a minority of cells rather than uniformly across the population.

ideas.title: Dilution-independent persistence test across cell divisions and quiescence
ideas.description: Label a stimulus-experienced population with a live AP-1 reporter and a division-tracking dye, then separate cells into quiescent and proliferating fractions over a long rest period. Measure whether AP-1-dependent accessibility and priming decay with division, dilution, or time alone, and compare the decay curve with that of stable marks such as DNA methylation or H3K4me1. This separates a true epigenetic memory from a transient signalling state that merely persists while the cell stays alive.

ideas.title: Chromatin conformation persistence after AP-1 activity ends
ideas.description: Perform Micro-C or Hi-C at AP-1-responsive loci at several timepoints after a stimulus is removed, and pair this with live-cell imaging of locus distance in reporter lines. Test whether enhancer-promoter loops formed by AP-1 remain after AP-1 is no longer bound, and whether these loops are required for faster re-induction. Persistent looping that outlasts AP-1 occupancy would indicate a structural memory layer, and disrupting the loops with CTCF or cohesin depletion would test whether that structure is necessary.
